front: Components of a commercial package policy (CPP)
back: Common Policy Declarations + Common Policy Conditions (IL 00 17) + interline endorsements + two or more coverage parts. One coverage part = monoline.
source: ISO IL 00 17 11 98; IRMI glossary 'commercial package policy'

back: Cancellation; Changes; Examination of Books and Records (up to 3 years after); Inspections and Surveys; Premiums (first Named Insured pays and receives return premium); Transfer of Rights and Duties (needs written consent, except on death of an individual named insured).
10 days for nonpayment of premium; 30 days for any other reason. Refund is pro rata if the insurer cancels; may be less than pro rata if the first Named Insured cancels.

front: CGL Supplementary Payments: bail bonds / loss of earnings
back: Up to $250 for bail bonds; actual loss of earnings up to $250 a day. Paid in addition to limits.

front: CGL Coverage C – Medical Payments time limit
back: Expenses must be incurred and reported within 1 year of the accident. Paid regardless of fault.

front: CGL General Aggregate vs Products-Completed Operations Aggregate
back: General aggregate = Coverage C + Coverage A (except products-completed ops) + Coverage B. Products-completed ops aggregate = Coverage A BI/PD in the products-completed operations hazard.

Lease of premises (not the fire-damage indemnity part); sidetrack agreement; easement/license (except construction within 50 ft of a railroad); municipal indemnity required by ordinance; elevator maintenance agreement; assumption of another's tort liability in a business contract.
Automatic, no charge. 60 days for unreported occurrences; 5 years for claims from occurrences reported within 60 days after the policy ends. No reinstated limits.
Written request within 60 days after the policy ends; premium up to 200% of annual premium; unlimited duration; starts after the basic ERP ends; reinstates aggregate limits.

Covers the owner (named insured) for BI/PD from the designated contractor's operations and the owner's general supervision. Ends when the work is completed or put to its intended use; premium refunds go to the contractor.

Vacant more than 60 consecutive days: no coverage for vandalism, sprinkler leakage (unless the system was protected against freezing), building glass breakage, water damage, theft or attempted theft; other covered losses reduced 15%. An owner's building is vacant unless at least 31% of its total square footage is rented/used for customary operations.

25% of paid loss plus deductible, plus up to an additional $25,000 per location (when the loss plus debris removal exceeds the limit or debris removal exceeds the 25%); must be reported within 180 days. Older editions: additional $10,000.

Fire dept service charge $1,000 (no deductible); pollutant clean-up $10,000 per 12 months; increased cost of construction lesser of $10,000 or 5%; electronic data $2,500; preservation of property 30 days.

Require 80%+ coinsurance. Newly acquired building $250,000 / BPP $100,000 (30 days); personal effects & property of others $2,500; valuable papers $2,500; off-premises $10,000; outdoor property $1,000 ($250 per tree); non-owned trailers $5,000; portable storage $10,000.
Begins 72 hours after loss for Business Income; immediately for Extra Expense. Extended Business Income: up to 60 days after operations resume.
Premises within 1 mile of the damaged property; Business Income starts 72 hours after the civil authority action and lasts up to 4 consecutive weeks.

Earliest of: expiration/cancellation, accepted by purchaser, interest ceases, construction abandoned, 90 days after completion, or 60 days after occupancy or intended use. Limit compared to value at completion.

front: Basic vs Broad vs Special causes of loss
back: Basic: fire, lightning, explosion, windstorm/hail, smoke, aircraft/vehicles, riot, vandalism, sprinkler leakage, sinkhole, volcanic. Broad adds falling objects; weight of snow, ice or sleet; water damage; collapse. Special = open perils.
A = loss to the undamaged portion; B = demolition cost; C = increased cost of construction.

front: Robbery vs safe burglary vs theft (crime)
back: Robbery: taking from a person by force or threat (or an obviously unlawful act they witness). Safe burglary: taking from a locked safe with marks of forcible entry, or taking the safe itself. Theft: any unlawful taking to the insured's deprivation.

front: Crime: loss sustained vs discovery tail
back: Loss sustained (CR 00 21): a loss sustained before cancellation can be discovered up to 1 year after cancellation. Discovery (CR 00 20): occurrence can be any time; 60 days after cancellation to discover. In both forms, this extended period ends immediately when replacement insurance takes effect, except that employee benefit plan losses keep 1 year after cancellation.
source: ISO CR 00 21 11 15, E.1.g; ISO CR 00 20 11 15, E.1.g (text reproduced in FC&S 'Commercial Crime Coverage Form', July 9, 2018); Rough Notes PF&M 251.4-2

back: Imports; exports; domestic shipments; instrumentalities of transportation and communication (bridges, tunnels, piers, pipelines, towers); personal property floaters; commercial property floaters. Michigan's own statutory definition of marine insurance is MCL 500.614 (1956); it covers similar risks and excludes buildings and their contents.
source: IMUA 'Nationwide Marine Definition'; MCL 500.614; NAIC Model 701 state chart (2021)

back: No abandonment; limit reinstated after loss (except total loss of a scheduled item); suit within 2 years of first knowledge of loss; valuation = least of ACV, restoration cost, or replacement cost.
Act of God, public enemy, act of the shipper, public authority, inherent vice. The carrier must also prove it was free of negligence.
source: Missouri Pacific R.R. v. Elmore & Stahl, 377 U.S. 134 (1964)

back: A Dwellings; B Other private structures; C Household personal property; D Loss of use; E Scheduled farm personal property; F Unscheduled farm personal property (80% coinsurance); G Other farm structures. Farm liability: H BI/PD, I P&AI, J Med pay.
source: ISO FP 00 10 09 94; FC&S 'Farm Liability Coverage Form' (2013)

back: Actual loss sustained for up to 12 consecutive months; no dollar limit; 72-hour waiting period; ordinary payroll for 60 days; Extended BI 60 days.

Replacement cost if the limit is at least 80% of RC; otherwise the greater of ACV or (limit / 80% of RC) x loss. RC is not paid until repair/replacement, except building repairs of $2,500 or less are settled on the RC basis even before repair.
Building +8% a year (prorated) unless another % is shown. BPP seasonal +25% if the BPP limit is at least 100% of average monthly values.

Fire dept $2,500; money orders/counterfeit $1,000; forgery $2,500; ICC $10,000; pollutant $10,000; dependent properties $5,000; fire extinguisher recharge $5,000; electronic data $10,000; computer interruption $10,000; fungi $15,000.
Products-completed ops aggregate and general aggregate each = 2 × the Liability and Medical Expenses limit. Professional services are excluded.
source: ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Sec. II D.4; B.1.j

back: Allowed if the building is vacant/unoccupied 60+ days, repairs not started within 30 days of loss payment, under a vacate/demolition order, fixtures being removed, or no utilities 30+ days / taxes unpaid over 1 year. In Michigan, state law requires the insurer to mail its cancellation notice at least 10 days before cancellation for both fire and casualty insurance.

P-1 automatic sprinkler system; P-2 automatic fire alarm; P-3 security service; P-4 private fire dept service contract; P-9 described system (the BOP version, BP 04 30, adds P-5 commercial cooking exhaust and extinguishing system). Fire is excluded if, before the fire, the insured knew of a suspension or impairment of a listed safeguard and didn't notify the insurer, or failed to keep a listed safeguard it controlled in complete working order. No notice is needed if a sprinkler system (BOP: also a P-5 system) shut off due to breakage, leakage, freezing or opened sprinkler heads is fully restored within 48 hours.

front: Utility Services: Direct Damage vs Time Element
back: BP 04 56 covers physical damage to covered property; BP 04 57 covers BI/Extra Expense, both from off-premises utility interruption. Overhead transmission lines are covered only if the Schedule shows them.
Covers liability for hired autos used by you or your employees, and non-owned autos (e.g., employees' cars) used in your business. Requires premium shown in Declarations.
Excess limits over underlying; drop down when underlying aggregates are exhausted; broader coverage for claims not covered by underlying, subject to a self-insured retention (SIR).
A: covers D&Os directly when the company can't or won't indemnify. B: reimburses the company for indemnifying D&Os. C: entity coverage (securities claims).
source: IRMI glossary (Side A; corporate reimbursement; entity securities coverage)

back: At least 10% of funds handled; minimum $1,000; maximum $500,000 ($1,000,000 if the plan holds employer securities). Covers fraud or dishonesty, not fiduciary errors.
Principal (who must perform, e.g., the contractor); obligee (who is protected, e.g., the owner); surety (who guarantees). The principal must reimburse the surety.
Bid bond: bidder will sign the contract and furnish bonds. Performance bond: contract will be completed. Payment bond: labor and material suppliers will be paid.

front: Michigan surplus lines tax and filings
back: 2% premium tax + 0.5% regulatory fee; sworn statements due Feb 15 and Aug 15. Self-procured insurance: insured reports within 30 days and pays the same.
In red ink, at least 10-point type: 'This insurance has been placed with an insurer that is not licensed by the state of Michigan. In case of insolvency, payment of claims may not be guaranteed.'

Michigan statute: capital and surplus of at least $1,500,000; $75,000 MI deposit or $1,000,000 US trust (Lloyd's-type $50,000,000); appoints the commissioner as agent for service of process. Note: since the federal NRRA (2010), U.S. nonadmitted insurers effectively need the greater of the home-state minimum or $15,000,000, and alien insurers qualify through the NAIC Quarterly Listing.

Single-family and 2-4 family: $250,000 building; residential contents $100,000. Other residential (5+ units): $500,000 building. Non-residential: $500,000 building / $500,000 contents. ICC up to $30,000 (building + ICC can't exceed the building maximum).
source: 44 CFR 61.6(a); 44 CFR Pt. 61 App. A(1) III.D; FEMA brochures (2024)

back: 30 days, except: purchase in connection with making, increasing, extending or renewing a loan (effective at loan closing, no wait); initial purchase within 13 months after a map revision takes effect (1-day wait); flooding on burned federal land (1-day wait if bought within 60 days of fire containment).
Member-owned liability insurer chartered in one state; members in similar businesses; liability coverage only; can't join state guaranty funds (required notice).
First-party: forensics, notification/call center, legal counsel, business interruption, extortion. Third-party: liability to affected consumers, regulatory inquiries.
